variants.name: Mule (Cudgel)
variants.description: The Mule is as much of a hodgepodge as its looks suggest. The Lionheart ship designers combined a good deal of cargo space with a decent amount of weaponry and even a fighter bay, and ended up with a ship that is mostly used as a freighter but can also be used as a warship because of its heavy armament and shields. This hodgepodge nature has its downside, though, namely its high crew requirement and the fact that any dedicated ship of the same cost will do better in a specialized role than the Mule will.

variants.name: Nest (Korath)
variants.description: Southbound Shipyards quickly answered the Free Worlds' call for a carrier by building modified cargo containers for Haulers - adding a pair of Fighter docking arms, some additional outfit space, and even a couple of bunks. Access to the fighters from within the ship is so inconvenient that most pilots opt to just stay aboard their fighters when in flight. While the technical name for this ship is "Hauler I: Type F," Southbound assembly workers started calling the single container variant the "Nest" due to its complement of Finch Fighters, and the name stuck.

The Osprey was the result. Although it is considered overpriced by most savvy pilots, it is nevertheless a perennial favorite among those who have the extra cash to spend on it.

variants.name: Outrider (Mark II)
variants.description: The Navy Outrider interceptor was decommissioned with the rise of the Navy Carrier. But after the bombing of Geminus saw the Navy's ability to construct new capital ships hindered, the Republic has requested production of the Outrider be resumed to support their fleets. 	No Navy license is required to purchase this ship. It was previously made available to the public via the surplus ship sales program on Geminus.

variants.name: Palisade (Hijacked)
variants.description: The largest in a series of ships the Syndicate promoted as an affordable mass transport solution, Palisades are well protected by heavy hull plating and massive shield emitters.

variants.name: Parapet (Spotlight)
variants.description: Prioritizing quantity over quality, the Parapet formed the baseline for a series of ships the Syndicate promoted as an affordable mass transport solution.

variants.name: Patrolboat (Turbo Blaster)
variants.description: The Patrolboat is an old ship that previously performed the role which the modern Gunboat fulfills. The main reason the Navy replaced it was the lack of a turret mount. Some retired Patrolboats have found a new role as merchant escorts or bounty hunters. 	This ship is exclusively offered as surplus inventory at the Geminus shipyards. If any are found for sale elsewhere, they were probably stolen.

variants.name: Pirate Drone (Modified)
variants.description: Locals started making these in their backyard garages to satisfy a limited demand for unofficial combat drones. From a distance, it looks like someone duct taped an energy blaster to the side of a civilian science drone. Upon closer inspection, that assessment isn't too far off. Each drone has minor differences in construction materials and how the wires are routed. Few pirates actually use these, but the ones who do tend to buy them in bulk.

variants.name: Plunder (Kludge Blaster)
variants.description: This ship is exclusively for sale to certain members of the Covert Mining Cartel. The Plunder is often mistaken for a modification of the Sunder currently sold by Syndicate Shipyards. But its lineage can be traced back to an older model that ceased production long ago. 	This confusion is exacerbated by the fact that the Plunder is indeed missing two of its original external cargo pods. However, these pods were located in the ship's undercarriage. Their removal allowed installation of a second drone bay. Unlike the second drone on the Syndicate's Sunder, this one faces forward, allowing it to quickly target the Plunder's prey.

variants.name: Protector (Korath)
variants.description: Voted the "ugliest ship in the sky" by Stars and Starships Magazine, the Protector is a typical example of brutally efficient Syndicate engineering. It is basically nothing more than eight turrets attached to a set of engines and crew's quarters, designed as a defense platform that can accompany merchant convoys.

variants.name: Rainmaker (Inferno Rockets)
variants.description: The Rainmaker is a missile boat built in the Republic Navy Yard. It comes equipped with four missile launchers and enough ammunition to destroy even ships many times its size. Because of their lack of maneuverability and relatively light shielding, Rainmakers serve best as long-range attack ships, and once their missile supply is spent, they are relatively useless in combat.

Missions: Inferno Dragon: Inferno Rockets Appear Patch

variants.name: Rancor (Berserker)
variants.description: The Rancor was originally a pirate vessel, and many were used in the early turf wars. The Alpha War was the beginning of the Rancor's decline as faster interceptors quickly outpaced and outmaneuvered this relatively slower ship. Today it is seen as a relic of the past, most noteworthy for influencing the design of the Fury.

variants.name: Raven (Hai)
variants.description: The Lionheart Raven is their most popular warship, an agile and elegant vessel that can nevertheless deal out and absorb considerable damage. Ravens are a favorite ship for bounty hunters, because they are more than a match for pirate interceptors and can be used by a skilled pilot to take down much larger ships as well.

variants.name: Roost (Korath)
variants.description: Southbound Shipyards' new fighter-carrying containers have created a new use for what many considered an outdated design. Four external fighter bays make this the biggest civilian carrier on the market, if a little awkward as a warship. After Southbound assembly workers successfully named the "Nest," "Hauler II: Type F" was quickly dubbed the "Roost" to continue the theme.

variants.name: Saber (Energy Cannons)
variants.description: During the caravan era, a boom of economic development spread along the paths of more heavily armed and technologically advanced merchant fleets originating from the Deep, which resulted in ships such as the Saber being developed. This medium warship was one of the powerhouses of military might in its time, armed to the teeth with five gun ports in the nose and a dorsal turret mount to fire at anything not in front of it. As pirates began to join together in larger war bands in response to the more heavily defended merchants, the Saber became popular amongst them as well. Unlike other ships such as the Firebird, it slowly faded out as competition rose, but it is nevertheless cherished by those who still own one.

variants.name: Scout (Bounty Hunter)
variants.description: The Lionheart Scoutship was designed back in the days when the galaxy was more sparsely populated, and ships prospecting for habitable worlds or worlds rich in resources would often travel far away from any habitable ports where they would be able to refuel. Although the galaxy has now been much more thoroughly explored, the Scout remains a popular ship for long-distance travel.

variants.name: Scrapper (Kludge Blaster)
variants.description: Rather than being a specific model of ship, the Scrappers are instead a family of vessels cobbled together from the remains of broken shuttles. On the rare occasion that Republic authorities bother to recognize their existence, Scrappers are treated as almost-illegal, patent-infringing death traps. Despite this, these ships are where many captains (and pirates) from poorer backgrounds get their start.

variants.name: Scrounger (Kludge Blaster)
variants.description: Assembled from the burned out remains of wrecked freighters, Scroungers are how some pilots lacking the funds for better options begin their careers. Unfortunately, it is not uncommon for those facing financial desperation to turn to small scale acts of piracy, scavenging parts and cargo from the scraps leftover by larger raiders.

variants.name: Shard (Smuggler)
variants.description: Megaparsec's Shard is a detachable excursion vessel marketed as a luxury yacht. 	Yachts do not come equipped with a hyperdrive. You cannot carry a yacht unless you have a ship in your fleet with a yacht bay.

variants.name: Shuttle (Derelict)
variants.description: Although Betelgeuse Shipyards produces other ship models as well, the majority of their profits come from sales of the Shuttle. This versatile ship serves equally well as a passenger transport or a cargo courier. It also happens to be the cheapest ship you can buy which is capable of hyperspace travel. 	Shuttles are not designed to withstand combat of any sort, but they are fast and maneuverable enough to get out of harm's way if attacked by a larger, slower ship. Although they are typically unarmed, they have enough space for one weapon, which is the origin of the popular phrase, "as useless as a blaster cannon on a shuttlecraft."

variants.name: Skein (Catalytic)
variants.description: This particular cockpit and engine set has found itself attached to three of Southbound Shipyards' new "Type F" Fighter-carrier pods. When the Free Worlds asked for a carrier, they did not expect one that would be able to carry almost as many fighters as the heaviest Navy warships. Given this fact, the Free Worlds have asked Southbound and Tarazed to restrict sale of the "Hauler III: Type F," "Skein" to its Militia only.

variants.name: Sliver (Smuggler)
variants.description: The Sliver was Megaparsec's attempt to enter the luxury space liner market. While it is no longer sold at their main shipyards, some Paradise Worlds keep them in stock for their wealthy clientel. Despite a superficial resemblance to the Splinter, the Sliver is notable for its distinctive ability to have up to three yachts dock with it. 	(These yachts are sold separately.)

variants.name: Sparrow (Afterburner)
variants.description: Classified as an interceptor rather than a fighter because it has its own hyperdrive instead of needing to be carried inside a larger ship, the Tarazed Sparrow is the smallest and cheapest combat ship available. Because of its limited cargo and passenger space, the primary way for a Sparrow pilot to pay the bills is to upgrade the weapons and hunt pirates... or become one. In either case, it is a perilous way to earn a living. 	Government reports indicate that as many as two out of every three first-time ship buyers who choose to pilot a Sparrow lose their ship (and often, their life as well) within the first month of owning it. Pilots who have survived longer than that tend to swear by replacing the stock weapons with missile launchers.

variants.name: Splinter (Inferno Rockets)
variants.description: The Splinter is the largest warship produced by the Megaparsec shipyard. It is designed to be faster and more maneuverable than other ships of a similar size, in order to serve as a heavy escort ship or as part of a planetary defense and patrol fleet. Because of its intended use in merchant convoys, it also has a fair amount of cargo space.

variants.name: Star Barge (Smuggler)
variants.description: The Syndicate CT-50 Star Barge is little more than a cluster of cargo containers with an engine at one end and a cockpit on the other. It is a slow and ugly ship, but it can carry enough cargo to earn its captain a steady income even in parts of the galaxy where it is hard to find passengers to carry or courier missions. 	Because they often carry valuable cargo, and because they are too slow to evade any attackers, Star Barges are a common target of pirates.

variants.name: Star Explorer (Biohazard)
variants.description: An ancient space exploration vessel from the early days of Hyperspace travel. Many claim the Star Explorer's design was heavily influenced by an old Earth science-fiction show as a marketing gimmick to entice young people to leave Sol and risk their lives exploring the vast unknown. Of the few that haven't been lost or destroyed, there are some still being used as actual science and exploration vessels. The rest are held in private collections by fans of antiquities.

variants.name: Star King (Hijacked)
variants.description: To celebrate a new era of peace in galactic history, Betelgeuse has brought the Star King back into production. An even larger luxury liner than their distinguished Star Queen, this vessel offers its passengers all of the high end amenities that wealthy travelers would expect from its smaller counterpart.

variants.name: Star King (Hai Engines)
variants.description: To celebrate a new era of peace in galactic history, Betelgeuse has brought the Star King back into production. An even larger luxury liner than their distinguished Star Queen, this vessel offers its passengers all of the high end amenities that wealthy travelers would expect from its smaller counterpart.

variants.name: Star Queen (Advanced Research)
variants.description: The Star Queen is a relic of a more peaceful period of galactic history: a luxury liner for high-end tourists. Every cabin has its own mini-bar, and the bathrooms have marble tile and showers that use actual hot water instead of chemicals or sonic vibrations. 	In support of environmental movements across the galaxy, all Star Queens come standard with an array of solar panels as their only source of energy as opposed to more popular power generators such as fuel cells or nuclear reactors that produce some amount of waste. Although some argue that this is a pointless move given the prevalence of clean fusion reactors, others have applauded it and cited the prohibitive costs of fusion reactors as a reason for using solar panels.

variants.name: Stingray (Blaster)
variants.description: With an empty hull weighing in at 180 tons, Megaparsec's Stingray is among the heaviest interceptors in the galaxy. They were once deployed by Syndicate security forces to escort freighter convoys and patrol trade routes, but the Syndicate has since replaced it with the more economically friendly Wasp. 	While some Stingrays can still be found protecting private merchant fleets or mining asteroids, many have found their way into the hands of pirates.

variants.name: Striker Drone (Kludge Blaster)
variants.description: Southbound Shipyards and Kraz Cybernetics hastily constructed this modified Surveillance Drone at the request of the Free Worlds. With barely enough weapon space to install anything larger than a small missile pod, the Striker drone can provide long distance fire support or aid in surprise tactical strikes.

variants.name: Sunder (Twin Blaster)
variants.description: The Sunder is a versatile mining platform equipped with dedicated prospecting equipment, most notably an undercarriage that supports two Mining Drones. The lineage of this ship can be traced back to the old asteroid mining ships used in the Sol Main Belt centuries ago; however, because of recent Syndicate efforts to further exploit the Core's mineral wealth, the newest model of the Sunder is now manufactured by Syndicated Shipyards.

variants.name: Sunracer (Atomic Afterburner)
variants.description: The ship of choice for most professional racing pilots. With a focus on maximizing speed, a Sunracer lacks space to spare for ubiquitous things like cargo, bunks, weapons, or a hyperdrive. 	These ships serve a unique niche and are exclusively sold at inflated prices on the planet they're named after. Although it's possible to squeeze one into a fighter bay, the prohibitive cost and minimal combat capability means there isn't a compelling reason to use them in that capacity.

variants.name: Quicksilver (Korath)
variants.description: The Megaparsec Quicksilver is a warship built around a single concept: to design the smallest and fastest ship capable of carrying two Particle Cannons. Because of its speed, reverse thrusters, and long weapons range, the Quicksilver can keep a safe distance from most targets and bombard them with particle bursts until they are destroyed. The focus on its weaponry left the Quicksilver with no room for even the most basic shield generator. Unfortunately the Headhunter eventually surpassed the original design intent, but the Quicksilver's better durability to cost ratio, and the existence of long-term contracts, has kept it in use with Syndicate security forces.

variants.name: Vanguard (Inferno Rockets)
variants.description: The Vanguard is Syndicated Systems' newest warship intended for the heavy anti-pirate defense market. Vanguards offer an unusual feature set, focusing on powerful fixed guns and featuring Syndicated Systems' latest automation technologies, resulting in an atypically low crew complement for a ship its size. Few capital ships will endure for long under the withering fusillade of gunfire that it can unleash against those in front of it.

variants.name: Volary (Heavy)
variants.description: The technology on the Volary, while in line with other modern ships, is surprisingly mundane for a newly constructed ship from Lionheart. This has caused some to speculate that the Deep has lost their edge in technological advancement. Alternatively, conspiracy theorists suggest that the Deep has been sitting on this design for some time and has only revealed it now in preparation for some threat unknown to the general public. Deep Security, for its part, has no comment on these rumors.

variants.name: War Hauler (Grudge Hammer)
variants.description: A leftover from the Alpha Wars, War Hauler production stopped soon after the wars ended. Although the ship predates the Republic and is not manufactured by any modern shipyards, Parliament still passed a law prohibiting retail sales of this ship to ordinary civilians. This has made the few remaining War Haulers on the secondary market a highly sought after item amongst collectors of antique ships.

variants.name: Wasp (Kludge Blaster)
variants.description: The Wasp is a medium-strength interceptor, designed by Syndicated Shipyards to serve as an escort for cargo vessels. Like most Syndicate ships, it is not particularly pretty, but it at least serves the purpose it was made for.

variants.name: Bulk Freighter(hai)
variants.description: The Bulk Freighter is the ultimate cargo ship, able to carry as much cargo as four ordinary Syndicate Freighters. Its on-board gearing allows it to service even the most primitive colonies, though dock workers in busier spaceports often joke that it would be simpler to carry smaller freighters within its gigantic holds. 	It is also an incredibly slow and difficult to maneuver ship, especially when loaded down with cargo. Some freight caravans use ordinary freighters instead of Bulk Freighters just to avoid the hassle of constantly having to wait for the Bulk Freighter to properly align itself for hyperspace travel.

variants.name: Mammoth (Insurgent Subjugation Gear)
variants.description: This is a rare, extensively modified Behemoth used by some pirates and smugglers to transport large amounts of goods to systems both near and far. It is armed well enough to handle even a Navy Frigate if caught and fast enough to dash away from anything bigger.

variants.name: Midnight Hauler VI (Hauler VI (prototype))
variants.description: After a series of delays due to unfortunate events in the testing phase, the Hauler VI is finally available for purchase. There were rumors that an innovative new refrigerated storage system was being developed for it. But no such system is present in the final production model.

variants.name: Missileboat (Rainmaker (Nuclear))
variants.description: For centuries, the Missileboat provided fleet admirals with a reliable artillery unit to support their front line vessels. The outdated systems interface on this ship have a higher crew requirement than the Rainmaker currently used by the Navy. Retired Missileboats are sometimes used by bounty hunters. 	This ship is exclusively offered as surplus inventory at the Geminus shipyards. If any are found for sale elsewhere, they were probably stolen.

variants.name: Missileboat (Rainmaker (Wanderer))
variants.description: For centuries, the Missileboat provided fleet admirals with a reliable artillery unit to support their front line vessels. The outdated systems interface on this ship have a higher crew requirement than the Rainmaker currently used by the Navy. Retired Missileboats are sometimes used by bounty hunters. 	This ship is exclusively offered as surplus inventory at the Geminus shipyards. If any are found for sale elsewhere, they were probably stolen.

variants.name: Scrapper (Turbo Blaster)
variants.description: Rather than being a specific model of ship, the Scrappers are instead a family of vessels cobbled together from the remains of broken shuttles. On the rare occasion that Republic authorities bother to recognize their existence, Scrappers are treated as almost-illegal, patent-infringing death traps. Despite this, these ships are where many captains (and pirates) from poorer backgrounds get their start.

variants.name: Scrounger (Turbo Blaster)
variants.description: Assembled from the burned out remains of wrecked freighters, Scroungers are how some pilots lacking the funds for better options begin their careers. Unfortunately, it is not uncommon for those facing financial desperation to turn to small scale acts of piracy, scavenging parts and cargo from the scraps leftover by larger raiders.

variants.name: Starcadia (Prototype)
variants.description: The technology on the Starcadia, while in line with other modern ships, is surprisingly mundane for a newly deployed ship from the Deep. This has caused some to speculate that the Deep has lost their edge in technological advancement. Alternatively, conspiracy theorists suggest that the Deep has been sitting on this design for some time and is only releasing it now in preparation for some threat unknown to the general public. Deep Security, for its part, has no comment on these rumors.

variants.name: Marauder Hauler (used)
variants.description: Some Haulers are modified to reduce mass and drag by replacing the standard cargo container with something smaller. The previous owner of this Hauler took the standard Southbound Shipyards cargo container and cut it down to half its size.

variants.description: The Argosy has long been a favorite ship for pirates, who have come up with many tricks for modifying them to be more suitable as warships.

variants.name: Marauder Bounder (Used)
variants.description: This Megaparsec Bounder has been modified from a courier-scout into a heavy escort interceptor - currently the largest in the class. A little extra outfit space, reinforced turret mounts, a new gun port in front of the pilot, and additional shield emitters grant this former transport both fearsome speed and armament.

variants.name: Marauder Raven (Used)
variants.description: Whoever modified this Raven has given more heft to an agile and elegant vessel. They've added a turret and some apparently-flimsy bulkheads over extra shield emitters and outfit space. If it weren't for the wings, the central hull would barely be recognizable as Lionheart's original under the patchwork that you expect has made an already deadly warship even more so.

variants.name: Missileboat (Used)
variants.description: For centuries, the Missileboat provided fleet admirals with a reliable artillery unit to support their front line vessels. The outdated systems interface on this ship have a higher crew requirement than the Rainmaker currently used by the Navy. Retired Missileboats are sometimes used by bounty hunters. 	This ship is exclusively offered as surplus inventory at the Geminus shipyards. If any are found for sale elsewhere, they were probably stolen.

variants.name: Patrolboat (Used)
variants.description: The Patrolboat is an old ship that previously performed the role which the modern Gunboat fulfills. The main reason the Navy replaced it was the lack of a turret mount. Some retired Patrolboats have found a new role as merchant escorts or bounty hunters. 	This ship is exclusively offered as surplus inventory at the Geminus shipyards. If any are found for sale elsewhere, they were probably stolen.

variants.name: Enforcer (Used)
variants.description: Prior to the formation of the galactic Republic, many star systems were owned by "governing corporate entities," with the vast majority of space being inaccessible to private citizens. The only exception to this rule were the pirate bands, whose few ships were often stolen or rebellious corporate fleets of their own, yet who had an outsized impact on interstellar trade. The necessity for corporations to protect their operations meant that Enforcer was one of the most common vessels used for security and defense. The ship boasts an armament of four gun ports and a turreted mount, all packed on a small but defensible frame that was powerful for its time. 	Although no longer on the market, the Enforcer finds itself in the possession of a small number of merchants and, ironically, various groups of pirates, as an aging combat ship easily outperformed by other light warships or even interceptors of a similar size.

variants.name: Modified Hogshead (Used)
variants.description: Occasionally a pirate gets the idea in his head to adapt a ship not designed for warfare into a pirate vessel. Oftentimes the results weren't worth the effort. But some of these attempts manage to find a niche. A Modified Hogshead might appear under the command of bounty hunters or slavers who are likely to find a ship of this type useful in their line of work. 	Over half the passenger space on this Hogshead has been gutted to make room for more shield emitters and weapon systems to power the two additional gun ports. Thick armored plating has been welded over the passenger viewports and other vulnerable areas of the hull, making the ship heavier, but more durable.

variants.name: Saber (Used)
variants.description: During the caravan era, a boom of economic development spread along the paths of more heavily armed and technologically advanced merchant fleets originating from the Deep, which resulted in ships such as the Saber being developed. This medium warship was one of the powerhouses of military might in its time, armed to the teeth with five gun ports in the nose and a dorsal turret mount to fire at anything not in front of it. As pirates began to join together in larger war bands in response to the more heavily defended merchants, the Saber became popular amongst them as well. Unlike other ships such as the Firebird, it slowly faded out as competition rose, but it is nevertheless cherished by those who still own one.

variants.name: Arcus FTL
variants.description: The Arcus is a hybrid transport-freighter designed for deep space exploration. It is intended to serve as the core upon which a colony station can be established and expanded upon. 	Merchant captains willing to pay the exhorbitant cost can employ this ship in mundane transport-freight operations.

variants.name: Arcus Derelict
variants.description: The Arcus is a hybrid transport-freighter designed for deep space exploration. It is intended to serve as the core upon which a colony station can be established and expanded upon. 	Merchant captains willing to pay the exhorbitant cost can employ this ship in mundane transport-freight operations.

variants.name: Castellanus (Military)
variants.description: The Castillanus heavy warship expands upon the design principles exhibited by the Nimbus. While it cannot match the raw offensive power of the Venta, the turret mounts make it a more versatile weapons platform.

variants.name: Castellanus (Mining)
variants.description: The Castillanus heavy warship expands upon the design principles exhibited by the Nimbus. While it cannot match the raw offensive power of the Venta, the turret mounts make it a more versatile weapons platform.

variants.name: Nimbo Cumulus (Military)
variants.description: A recently developed upgrade to the Nimbo Stratus. With it's extra gun port and weapon capacity, some regard the Cumulus as a light warship. The Hicemus are closely monitoring how the ship performs to determine whether or not it needs to be placed under their licensing restrictions.

variants.name: Nimbus FTL Midnight
variants.description: The Nimbus is the first spaceship that the Incipias built that was truly able to navigate through a system. Since it was first manufactured it has been cherished among wealthier captains and a dream of captains just starting out. 	Although the Nimbus is labeled as a medium warship, it is multipurpose; whether one uses it for mining, passenger transport or cargo, it will perform its job nicely. It is only occasionally used in combat because the Incipias are not currently fighting open wars.

variants.name: Maeri'het (Cloak Armor 10)
variants.description: The Maeri is the smallest Het ship created by the Builders' stations, a prime example of the genetic technology they once possessed. Its small size is compensated by the fact that it can hide its location from most types of sensors.

variants.name: Maeri'het (Cloak Armor 20)
variants.description: The Maeri is the smallest Het ship created by the Builders' stations, a prime example of the genetic technology they once possessed. Its small size is compensated by the fact that it can hide its location from most types of sensors.

variants.name: Telis'het (Tactical Armor 10)
variants.description: When the Builders designed the exoskeleton of the Telis, they came to the conclusion that it would have been impossible to make it resilient enough without compromising its agility and integrity. Instead, they focused heavily on improving their shield technology, giving the Telis many of their regenerators.

variants.name: Vareti'het (Durable Armor 20)
variants.description: The Vareti was the strongest Het the Builders were able to complete, starting its mass production only a year before the beginning of the invasion. It relies on shield matrixes even more than its little brothers, using larger and more effective restorers that were developed alongside this project.

variants.name: Rao'xeris (Key Stone)
variants.description: A deep space mining vessel, the Rao'xeris was used to transport materials harvested in the northern reaches of Builder space to processing facilities in the southern region. When the Ka'het invasion began, many found that it could easily be converted into a combat warship. 	This ship is capable of diving into the harsh atmosphere of a gas giant.

variants.name: Akfir A'awoj (Civilian)
variants.description: The largest of Korath production vessels are derived from a common and ancient chassis. This utility vessel was converted into a warship early in the Korath civil war, but was quickly outclassed as the war intensified. It is named after a world that vanished from Korath space. Nir Akfir may still exist in the territory of another species. If it does, they probably refer to it by a different name.

variants.name: Akfir A'awoj (Jump Limited)
variants.description: The largest of Korath production vessels are derived from a common and ancient chassis. Missions: Midnight Gorgon Heliarch Scouting - Peripheral Repair Hub

variants.name: Far'itar (Jump)
variants.description: Dedicated cargo transports are no longer necessary among the Korath Exiles. Rather than being scrapped, these ships have been repurposed to serve as mobile prisons. Criminals convicted of serious crimes are given a choice between a quick death via a microbot nutrigel processor or a life long assignment working on a Far'itar mining vessel. Prisoners who fail to perform their duties are still eligible for being tossed into the nutrigel processor. 	Operating these vessels can be lucrative for its captains, but the Korath authorities require them to activate their self destruct in the event of a mutiny or other event that could result in a prisoner escape. Whether or not they have the fortitude to fulfill this duty is put to the test whenever they engage in a boarding battle.

variants.name: Kar'iyar (Ember)
variants.description: The Kar'iyar is a lightly armed fighter transport ship. They primarily serve as escorts to supplement the fire power of larger Korath fleets.

variants.name: Kar'iyar (Hyperdrive)
variants.description: The Kar'iyar is a lightly armed fighter transport ship. They primarily serve as escorts to supplement the fire power of larger Korath fleets.

variants.name: Sa'ifar (Firelight B)
variants.description: A Sa'ifar houses a multitude of samples representing all natural life that could be salvaged from Korath worlds before they were ruined by the war. The crews operating these vessels fervently hope that their preservation efforts will one day contribute to the restoration of their ancient worlds.

variants.name: Tch'esar (Damaged Jump Drive)
variants.description: Tch'esar warships are no longer regarded as suitable for serious combat. However, they are still a capable platform for some of the Korath's heavier guns. The few which haven't been dismantled for scrap are utilized as patrol vessels and escorts to bolster the Korath home defense fleets.

variants.name: Tubfalet (flip)
variants.description: The venerable Palavret has been a mainstay of the Korath raiding fleet, elements of its design dating back from before the era of shortages and desperation caused by a life in exile. Over forty generations of raiders have terrorized neighboring systems over the centuries. 	Constant warfare against surrounding aliens has been building pressure on Korath shipyards to recover some of their ancient prowess. Now, with a fresh industrial network to draw upon, the Korath have created a new raider to deal with modern targets, and the Tubfalet-Class Raiding Ship is named for an admiral who dealt with such enemies. Despite extensive injuries, he remained on his flag bridge during a Remnant attack, leading his squadron to victory.

variants.name: Palavret (Korath Raider (Torpedo))
variants.description: Successive raider designs have been the Korath warship of choice for plundering neighboring species for generations. Named for a celebrated captain who gave her life to ensure her crippled vessel made it back to port with its desperately needed cargo of stolen fish, the Palavret-Class Raiding Ship continues that grim tradition. 	Like all Exile ships, the Palavret has been adapted to house as many Korath as possible, as comfortably as possible, inflating its size beyond similarly armed warships. The spaceborne construction techniques employed allow for the ship's easy replacement, facilitating continued raids of nearby systems.

variants.name: Rano'erek (Civilian Scavenger)
variants.description: After the Korath were exiled from their homelands, efficient resource collection became a priority. World-ships were too precious to risk on dangerous forays, and raiders lacked the cargo capacity. The Rano'erek-class Asteroid Dredging Ship, named for a respected civilian politician and economist, was born as an answer to this problem. 	Featuring an abundance of cargo and passenger space in addition to their formidable defensive armament, these bulky ships can also offer potent support for frontline Palavrets.

variants.name: Rano'erek (Digger Scavenger)
variants.description: After the Korath were exiled from their homelands, efficient resource collection became a priority. Featuring an abundance of cargo and passenger space in addition to their formidable defensive armament, these bulky ships can also offer potent support for frontline Palavrets.

variants.name: Kas'lor Ik 582 (Shock Strike)
variants.description: The largest of Korath production vessels are derived from a common and ancient chassis. This relatively streamlined ship has been adapted to collect, refine, and transport hyperspace fuel. Its name refers to the delicious squids that lived in their gas giants, and especially Deka Dathnak.

variants.name: Lor'nag Ik 590 (Shock Strike)
variants.description: The largest of Korath production vessels are derived from a common and ancient chassis. This bulbous ship has been adapted to carry passengers between stations, or boarding parties into enemy strongholds. Its name is in memory of the Anatruskor, who invented the jump drive.

variants.name: Ra'gru Ik 618 (Shock Strike)
variants.description: The largest of Korath production vessels are derived from a common and ancient chassis. This deceptively spindly ship bristles with weapon emplacements for heavy raiding or defending other vessels. It is named after the Mereti's capital planet, where they made powerful warships out of modular components.

variants.name: Ra'at Ik 621 (Shock Strike)
variants.description: The largest of Korath production vessels are derived from a common and ancient chassis. This many-lobed ship has been adapted to carry fighters into large-scale raids, or mining craft into asteroid belts. Its radial arrangements of hangars allows fighters a maximum variety of safe approach patterns in combat. Sestor exiles, who had a great affinity for carriers and fighters, bequeathed this variant its name after their capital world.

variants.name: Ikatila'ej (Thermal Obliterator)
variants.description: For most of their manufacturing needs, the Korath rely, as even some terrestrial species do, upon their space station and asteroid infrastructure. Due to their spacebound existence, however, the acceptability for failure and downtime is slim to nonexistent. Should equipment aboard a station or a world-ship fail, the Ikatila'ej, named for an inventor famously proficient in a variety of fields, is called in to provide critical support. Its microbot-run factory produces basic living supplies, machine parts, and systems cores, and may assist in continuing stalled production. 	When not assisting with damaged ships and stations, or replenishing its own stores, the Ikatila'ej serves as an all-in-one recycling, mining, refining, and factory ship, using its microbot-powered grinder to rapidly turn asteroids and garbage into whatever products the civilian economic planning committees have determined to be in the most dire need.

variants.name: Korsmanath A'awoj (Jump)
variants.description: Korsmanath A'awojs, named in memory of the Korath home system, are massive nomadic habitats that hold much of their remaining population. True flying cities, they could be self-contained miniature worlds were it not for their heavy defensive armament and reliance on unsustainable materials, methods, and sources of power. 	Commission of new Korsmanath A'awojs is a resource-demanding, labor-intensive, painstaking process fraught with political intrigue. Navarchs fight with the civilian government for resources and yard time they would rather devote to building raiding and defensive fleets, civilians vie with each other for a place on the next ship, and planning committees argue with engineers over what methods and technologies to use. This leads to construction delays, corner-cutting, and over-militarization of the design at best, and violent feuds at worst.

variants.name: Tek Far 71 - Lek (Jump)
variants.description: The Kor Sestor war fleets rely heavily on small, powerful fighters and drones. This ship can carry up to ten of their drones, clamped to the exterior of its hull.

variants.name: Tek Far 78 - Osk (Jump)
variants.description: This carrier is equipped with docking clamps for up to nine fighters. When loaded with a full complement of the powerful Kor Sestor robotic fighters, it is a formidable opponent.

Missions: Midnight Wanderers: Sestor: Final Revenge B

variants.name: Kar Ik Vot 349 (Secured)
variants.description: The largest and deadliest of the Kor Sestor robotic warships, a single one of these battlecruisers can hold its own against an entire fleet of lesser ships.

variants.name: Tek Far 109 (Secured)
variants.description: The TF109 is designed almost solely for the purpose of carrying a fleet of Kor Sestor fighters and drones. Without them to serve as a protective screen, the ship itself is relatively helpless.

variants.name: Met Par Tek 53 (Secured)
variants.description: Although this is the smallest Kor Sestor ship other than their fighters, it is larger than most human capital ships and considerably more powerful.

variants.name: Model 8 (Secured)
variants.description: The primary role of the smallest Kor Mereti drones is asteroid mining, but their lasers can also be employed as offensive weapons when necessary.

variants.name: Model 16 (Secured)
variants.description: The Kor Mereti war drones are constructed in a modular fashion, which allows them to grow over time as more materials become available. This one is recently built, and relatively small.

variants.name: Model 32 (Secured)
variants.description: The Kor Mereti built their drones to mimic life: capable of growth and development throughout their life cycles. Their automated factories can convert the drones from one configuration to another by adding or removing modules.

variants.name: Model 64 (Secured)
variants.description: This medium-sized drone serves the Kor Mereti fleets in much the same way as a human Frigate, but in terms of total firepower it is far beyond anything humans have constructed.

variants.name: Model 128 (Secured)
variants.description: As Kor Mereti drones continue to grow and develop into their final form, they split down the middle. At the same time, their shielding and weaponry continue to become stronger.

variants.name: Model 256 (Secured)
variants.description: There is a saying among the Quarg that every species which insists on studying war will eventually construct a weapon that outlives its creators. For the Korath, their war drones have very nearly done so.

variants.name: Model 512 (Secured)
variants.description: This is the final state in the evolution of a Kor Mereti war drone: a perfect ring, with incredibly powerful shields and turrets firing in every direction.

variants.name: Palavret (Korath Raider (Fireswarm))
variants.description: Successive raider designs have been the Korath warship of choice for plundering neighboring species for generations. Named for a celebrated captain who gave her life to ensure her crippled vessel made it back to port with its desperately needed cargo of stolen fish, the Palavret-Class Raiding Ship continues that grim tradition. 	Like all Exile ships, the Palavret has been adapted to house as many Korath as possible, as comfortably as possible, inflating its size beyond similarly armed warships. The spaceborne construction techniques employed allow for the ship's easy replacement, facilitating continued raids of nearby systems.

variants.name: Paragon Zibruka (Pug Paragon Zibruka)
variants.description: The Zibruka is the smallest Pug warship that you know of. It is a fearsome ship to face off against, especially in swarms. 	The Paragon variant of the Zibruka is intended for battles rated tier 2 and above. It has increased shielding and a reinforced hull. It also adds a turret mount and the additional space to use it.

variants.name: Pug Zibruka (Seeker)
variants.description: The Zibruka is the smallest Pug warship that you know of. Despite having only two gun ports, its two advanced guns combined with its fast and efficient engine systems make it a fearsome ship to face off against, especially in swarms.

variants.name: Pug Enfolta (Seeker)
variants.description: The Enfolta is a medium-sized Pug warship. It has a formidable armament of advanced weaponry supported by powerful integrated energy generation. A single Enfolta can take on multiple smaller human ships.

variants.name: Pug Enfolta (Zapper)
variants.description: The Enfolta is a medium-sized Pug warship. It has a formidable armament of advanced weaponry supported by powerful integrated energy generation. A single Enfolta can take on multiple smaller human ships.

variants.name: Pug Maboro (Seeker)
variants.description: The Maboro appears to be the Pug's capital warship. Its shield matrix and hull are much weaker than human capital ships; however, it is able to regenerate its shields quickly. Its fearsome ordnance and advanced anti-missile defenses make it a ship that only the strongest human capital ships are able to oppose.

variants.name: Pug Maboro (Zapper)
variants.description: The Maboro appears to be the Pug's capital warship. Its shield matrix and hull are much weaker than human capital ships; however, it is able to regenerate its shields quickly. Its fearsome ordnance and advanced anti-missile defenses make it a ship that only the strongest human capital ships are able to oppose.

variants.name: Tubfalet (Korath Raider (Chaos Hammer))
variants.description: The venerable Palavret has been a mainstay of the Korath raiding fleet, elements of its design dating back from before the era of shortages and desperation caused by a life in exile. Over forty generations of raiders have terrorized neighboring systems over the centuries. 	Constant warfare against surrounding aliens has been building pressure on Korath shipyards to recover some of their ancient prowess. Now, with a fresh industrial network to draw upon, the Korath have created a new raider to deal with modern targets, and the Tubfalet-Class Raiding Ship is named for an admiral who dealt with such enemies. Despite extensive injuries, he remained on his flag bridge during a Remnant attack, leading his squadron to victory.

variants.name: Armor Beetle (Arctic Dragon)
variants.description: The Armor Beetle is a specialized Unfettered warship that has been optimized for combat at the expense of cargo space.

variants.name: Prefect's Albatross (Albatross (Night Sword))
variants.description: Once they left human space, it became apparent to the Remnant that they would need to build their own shipyards in order to defend themselves if they were discovered by the Alphas or any other unfriendly faction. Using new composite materials that they discovered, they built ships very different from anything seen in human space. The wings of this Albatross sweep back, giving it a sleek appearance. This marks it as a Prefect's Albatross, used on the rare occasion when a Prefect isn't riding on a cloaked ship.

variants.name: Marauder Kestrel (Kestrel (Bloodwind))
variants.description: Several years ago, while visiting a sweat lodge in search of spiritual renewal, Tarazed's chief ship designer fell into a trance and journeyed to a reality separate from our own. There he saw visions of a strange and elegant starship. Returning to his work with renewed purpose, he spent the next seven years making the Kestrel a reality.

variants.name: Archon (Surveillance)
variants.description: The Archon's presence is chilling. The "ship" has an almost organic appearance, but your ship's scanners give you no discernible information on its construction. What exactly it is you do not know, but you can feel that it is powerful.

Missions: Midnight Lost Orphan: Warden of Atrocity

variants.name: Quarg Lindwyrm (Void Scraper)
variants.description: The Quarg use the Lindwyrm as a heavy freighter, transporting in its ample cargo bays items both mundane and fantastical. In the days before the advent of modern cargo scanners revealed some measure of their contents, "the inside of a Quarg cargo hold" was slang used to describe any thing or place thought to be unknowable.

variants.name: Quarg Drake (Explorer)
variants.description: The Drake is an older ship used by the Quarg for reconnaissance and initial contact with emerging spacefaring species. A popular legend states that a Drake surveyed Sol while humans began to discover spaceflight.

variants.name: Quarg Zilant (Void Scraper)
variants.description: The Zilant is a fast assault ship used to harass and break enemy fleet formations or make quick strikes on targets behind enemy lines. In more peaceful regions of the galaxy, they are relegated to simple patrol and escort duties.

variants.name: Quarg Wardragon (Scanner)
variants.description: The Wardragon is used by the Quarg as a light warship. It is an older design within the Quarg's fleets, supposedly less intimidating compared to their larger warships and thus more suitable for dealings with particularly nascent species.

variants.name: Quarg Wardragon (Void Scraper)
variants.description: The Wardragon is used by the Quarg as a light warship. It is an older design within the Quarg's fleets, supposedly less intimidating compared to their larger warships and thus more suitable for dealings with particularly nascent species.

variants.name: Quarg Wyvern (Explorer)
variants.description: When humans first encountered Quarg vessels, with their bizarre, scaly-looking hulls and alien forms, the comparisons to dragons of different sorts rapidly proliferated. The Wyvern is a midsize warship of the Quarg, though the distinction between the Quarg warship classes is insignificant to all but the most powerful forces in the galaxy.

variants.name: Quarg Typhon (Bloodstone)
variants.description: Typhons are old freighters the Quarg use mostly to transport materials in bulk.

variants.name: Quarg Typhon (Bloodstone Drive)
variants.description: Typhons are old freighters the Quarg use mostly to transport materials in bulk.

variants.name: Quarg Zahhak (Bloodstone Drive)
variants.description: The Zahhak is a Quarg utility support ship for extended deep space operations.

variants.name: Quarg Zahhak (Bloodstone)
variants.description: The Zahhak is a Quarg utility support ship for extended deep space operations.

variants.name: Quarg Naga (Bloodstone)
variants.description: The Naga was a mining vessel dating back to the pre-ringworld era.

variants.name: Quarg Skylark (Scanner)
variants.description: The Skylark is used by the Quarg as a freighter and warship.

variants.name: Quarg Skythrush (Scanner)
variants.description: The Skythrush was designed to be used as a blockade runner. Over a thousand years have passed since anyone has dared lay siege to the Quarg, shifting their role towards cargo support and scouting.

variants.name: Quarg Warkite (Scanner)
variants.description: The Warkite is a nimble assault ship used by the Quarg to harass and break enemy fleet formations or make quick surgical strikes against targets behind enemy lines.

variants.name: Kestrel (Modified Kestrel (Remnant Bays))

variants.name: Modified Bactrian (Remnant)
variants.description: The owner of this Bactrian has replaced some of it's armored hull plating with additional shield emitters. This has made the ship lighter and faster. An additional fighter can be carried on a landing pad on the roof.

variants.name: Raptor Prototype (unarmed)
variants.description: The Raptor Prototype is the result of experiments utilizing biological specimens collected from across the galaxy and beyond. As a result, its design is a bit different from other Remnant ships.

variants.name: Shrike (Thrasher)
variants.description: The Shrike is a nimble gunship that is usually outfitted to provide long distance fire support. Remnant captains embarking on solo missions might opt for a more aggressive outfit selection instead.

variants.name: Shrike (disarmed)
variants.description: The Shrike is a nimble gunship that is usually outfitted to provide long distance fire support. Remnant captains embarking on solo missions might opt for a more aggressive outfit selection instead.

variants.name: Wren (Research)
variants.description: Thanks to its cloaking technology, the Wren provides discreet transportation to remote Remnant research outposts. 	The cloaking technology is built into the Wren's hull; it cannot be removed or transferred to another ship.

variants.name: Wren (Gravedigger)
variants.description: Thanks to its cloaking technology, the Wren provides discreet transportation to remote Remnant research outposts. 	The cloaking technology is built into the Wren's hull; it cannot be removed or transferred to another ship.

variants.name: Shadow Falcon (B)
variants.description: This Tarazed Falcon has had some modifications done. The hull has built in jamming, scan interference, and enhanced heat dissipation. Whoever designed this seemed to be intent on creating a stealth warship.

variants.name: Shadow Hawk (B)
variants.description: This Tarazed Hawk has had some modifications done. The hull has built in jamming, scan interference, and enhanced heat dissipation. Whoever designed this seemed to be intent on creating a stealth warship.

variants.name: Shadow Osprey (B)
variants.description: This Tarazed Osprey has had some modifications done. The hull has built in jamming, scan interference, and enhanced heat dissipation. Whoever designed this seemed to be intent on creating a stealth interceptor.

variants.name: Shadow Raven (B)
variants.description: This Lionheart Raven has had some modifications done. The hull has built in jamming, scan interference, and enhanced heat dissipation. Whoever designed this seemed to be intent on creating a stealth warship.

variants.name: Falcon (Remnant B)
variants.description: The Tarazed Falcon is one of the most powerful warships that civilians can buy, a sleeker and more maneuverable alternative to the venerable and somewhat outdated Leviathan.

variants.name: Falcon (Remnant)
variants.description: The Tarazed Falcon is one of the most powerful warships that civilians can buy, a sleeker and more maneuverable alternative to the venerable and somewhat outdated Leviathan.

variants.name: Hawk (Remnant B)
variants.description: The Tarazed Hawk is an interceptor-class warship often used as an escort for freighters or in a planetary militia's patrol squadron. Hawks are fast enough to chase down most smaller ships, but are capable of mounting much more powerful weapons. They are also, of course, a favorite ship of pirate captains who have earned enough money to afford one.

variants.name: Hawk (Remnant)
variants.description: The Tarazed Hawk is an interceptor-class warship often used as an escort for freighters or in a planetary militia's patrol squadron. Hawks are fast enough to chase down most smaller ships, but are capable of mounting much more powerful weapons. They are also, of course, a favorite ship of pirate captains who have earned enough money to afford one.

variants.name: Osprey (Remnant B)
variants.description: After the Blackbird gained surprising popularity as an agile light warship despite its original design as a transport, Tarazed decided to produce a new design specifically intended as a warship. The Osprey was the result. Although it is considered overpriced by most savvy pilots, it is nevertheless a perennial favorite among those who have the extra cash to spend on it.

variants.name: Osprey (Remnant)

The Osprey was the result. Although it is considered overpriced by most savvy pilots, it is nevertheless a perennial favorite among those who have the extra cash to spend on it.

variants.name: Raven (Remnant B)
variants.description: The Lionheart Raven is their most popular warship, an agile and elegant vessel that can nevertheless deal out and absorb considerable damage. Ravens are a favorite ship for bounty hunters, because they are more than a match for pirate interceptors and can be used by a skilled pilot to take down much larger ships as well.

variants.description: Once they left human space, it became apparent to the Remnant that they would need to build their own shipyards in order to defend themselves if they were discovered by the Alphas or any other unfriendly faction. Using new composite materials that they discovered, they built ships very different from anything seen in human space.

variants.name: Starling (Gravedigger)
variants.description: One of the strangest and most useful things that the Remnant have discovered in the abandoned worlds of the Ember Waste is alien cloaking technology. They have designed their scout ships to cloak when needed in order to explore alien territory without being seen... or to escape in a hurry after stealing something particularly valuable from those aliens. 	The cloaking technology is built into the Starling's hull; it cannot be removed or transferred to another ship.

variants.name: Starling (Research)
variants.description: One of the strangest and most useful things that the Remnant have discovered in the abandoned worlds of the Ember Waste is alien cloaking technology. They have designed their scout ships to cloak when needed in order to explore alien territory without being seen... or to escape in a hurry after stealing something particularly valuable from those aliens. 	The cloaking technology is built into the Starling's hull; it cannot be removed or transferred to another ship.

variants.name: Gull (Gravedigger)
variants.description: While the Starling was the first successful ship to use technology derived from alien ruins, the Gull is the most recent. The current increase in Korath activities has caused foraging for resources to become a risky endeavor, forcing the Remnant to develop a specialized freighter for hauling cargo from remote sites without revealing their presence to hostile aliens. 	The Gull has quickly proven its worth, allowing the Starling fleets to return to riskier activities while the Gull takes over the hazardous convoy routes. It is now the primary element of the Remnant's extra-territorial resource operations. 	The cloaking technology is built into the Gull's hull; it cannot be removed or transferred to another ship.

variants.name: Gull (Research)
variants.description: While the Starling was the first successful ship to use technology derived from alien ruins, the Gull is the most recent. It is now the primary element of the Remnant's extra-territorial resource operations. 	The cloaking technology is built into the Gull's hull; it cannot be removed or transferred to another ship.

variants.name: Penguin (Gravedigger)
variants.description: Inspired by close contact with void sprites and the reinvigoration of xenobiology, the Penguin is a prototype designed to serve the dual roles of testing new starship technology while exploring hostile planets throughout the Ember Waste. One of this ship's distinguishing features is that it is truly alive and has a mind that approaches self-awareness. 	The cloaking technology is built into the Penguin's hull; it cannot be removed or transferred to another ship.

variants.name: Pelican (disarmed)
variants.description: The Pelican is closely based on the original semi-organic materials the Remnant found in the Ember Waste. While they are not technically alive, their internal mechanisms and method of construction bear such a close resemblance to living organisms that they are often considered as such. One key feature of this living resemblance is the innate sensory capabilities they possess, akin to sensor suites less advanced ships require for detailed scanning. These ships serve as the backbone of Remnant bulk salvage efforts, as well as their fast-logistics distribution network.

Missions: Grave Digger: Graveyard Robbery Job A
Grave Digger: Graveyard Robbery Job B
Grave Digger: Graveyard Robbery Job C

variants.name: Ibis (disarmed)
variants.description: The Ibis is a multipurpose carrier that serves as a mobile mining platform, an escort ship for Pelican fleets, and a combat platform using Terns for screening. It is capable of fielding a single wing of support craft, consisting of two Petrels and four Terns. 	The Ibis was designed shortly after the Albatross as a means of extending the range of resource collection efforts after the Remnant realized that an Alpha invasion might not be as imminent as originally believed.

Missions: Grave Digger: Graveyard Robbery Job A

variants.name: vyu-Ira (wounded)
variants.description: The vyu-Ir is an ancient ship of the Vyu, one of several chambers of the Rulei. It is not known whether or not this was their final ship-class, or one of many, but the technology found on it may represent the height of the Rulei's advancements, as well as the cause of their downfall.

variants.name: Modified Argosy (Sheragi Counterfeit)
variants.description: The Argosy has long been a favorite ship for pirates, who have come up with many tricks for modifying them to be more suitable as warships.

variants.name: Marauder Raven (Sheragi Counterfeit)
variants.description: Whoever modified this Raven has given more heft to an agile and elegant vessel. They've added a turret and some apparently-flimsy bulkheads over extra shield emitters and outfit space. If it weren't for the wings, the central hull would barely be recognizable as Lionheart's original under the patchwork that you expect has made an already deadly warship even more so.

variants.name: Marauder Vanguard (Sheragi Counterfeit)
variants.description: This Syndicate Shipyards Vanguard has been customized with additional armored plating as well as upgraded shielding to accommodate the latest experimental technologies.

variants.name: Diamondback (Berserker)
variants.description: Diamondbacks have been in use since explorers first settled the galactic rim. They've fought in various wars throughout the centuries and few survive to this day. Those that have are so extensively customized that no two are alike. Some southern legends claim the Diamondbacks were wrecked spacecraft created by extinct aliens and salvaged by early explorers such as Han Sizer. There is no evidence to support these claims and no reputable scholar takes them seriously.

variants.description: Diamondbacks have been in use since explorers first settled the galactic rim. They've fought in various wars throughout the centuries and few survive to this day. Those that have are so extensively customized that no two are alike. Some southern legends claim the Diamondbacks were wrecked spacecraft created by extinct aliens and salvaged by early explorers such as Han Sizer. There is no evidence to support these claims and no reputable scholar takes them seriously.

variants.name: Kvelqde-Sosrue (Stealth)
variants.description: This Kvelqde variant is designed to optimize the use of "Myiara" Fire Spouts. There are whispers that those who pilot such vessels are patron servants of a secret House that manipulates events from the shadows. Within the respectable echelons of Successor society such tales are dismissed as mere superstition, no more real than the monster from a children's poem. 	This ship can mount High House Multimodal Armor configurations. With an adaptor, it can also utilize Predecessor Multimode Armor materials.

variants.description: This variant Stolsaqra is a variant developed by Shadow House. Like the Kvelqde-Sosrue, it is designed to accomodate a pair of "Myiara" Fire Spouts into its arsenal. 	This ship can mount High House Multimodal Armor configurations. With an adaptor, it can also utilize Predecessor Multimode Armor materials.

variants.description: This variant Stolsaqra is a variant developed by Shadow House. Like the Kvelqde-Sosrue, it is designed to accomodate a pair of "Myiara" Fire Spouts into its arsenal. 	This ship can mount High House Multimodal Armor configurations. With an adaptor, it can also utilize Predecessor Multimode Armor materials.

variants.name: Myaede-Sosrue (Pristine)
variants.description: The Myaede-Sosrue incorporates durable hull plating that allows it to dive deep beneath the surface of oceanic environments. It loses its regular gun ports, but like other Shadow House variants, it is designed to accomodate a pair of "Myiara" Fire Spouts into its arsenal. 	This ship can mount High House Multimodal Armor configurations. With an adaptor, it can also utilize Predecessor Multimode Armor materials.

variants.name: Kvelqde-Kiitaa (OC)
variants.description: Many of the features of this Kvelqde have been scaled back, allowing it to be carried within a fighter bay without compromising its durability.

variants.name: Kvelqde-Kiitaa (Coilgun Turret)
variants.description: Many of the features of this Kvelqde have been scaled back, allowing it to be carried within a fighter bay without compromising its durability.

variants.name: Kvelqde-Khora (Nefa Coilguns)
variants.description: One of the more industrious members of the People's Houses has done their best to ruggedize this Kvelqde: additional armor plating has been laid over most of the exposed hull, a second gun port has been attached to the underside, and the shield grid has had its capacity substantially increased. While not quite capable of standing toe-to-toe with a production interceptor of the High Houses, it bares enough teeth for a bit of light piracy, and its greater durability is quite welcome for navigating the decaying stations and hostile worlds of southwestern Successor space.

variants.name: Stolsaqra (Fajet Coilguns)
variants.description: The Successors have limited experience in making warships this small, and while their attempt at an interceptor is durable and sports a surprising amount of firepower for a ship of its size, it is also plagued with power and propulsion issues, as most of their standard technology is either too large or not powerful enough to yield effective combat performance at this scale. The result is a ship that ambitious pilots call a challenge and prudent captains call a deathtrap, but that continues to see use as a patrol and escort vessel because of its speed and heavy armament. 	The Stolsaqra also has the distinction of being the only purpose-built warship manufactured by the High Houses that is made available to the general public, albeit with significantly downgraded systems compared to the military-exclusive model.

variants.name: Stolsaqra (Nejet Coilguns)
variants.description: The Successors have limited experience in making warships this small, and while their attempt at an interceptor is durable and sports a surprising amount of firepower for a ship of its size, it is also plagued with power and propulsion issues, as most of their standard technology is either too large or not powerful enough to yield effective combat performance at this scale. The result is a ship that ambitious pilots call a challenge and prudent captains call a deathtrap, but that continues to see use as a patrol and escort vessel because of its speed and heavy armament. 	The Stolsaqra also has the distinction of being the only purpose-built warship manufactured by the High Houses that is made available to the general public, albeit with significantly downgraded systems compared to the military-exclusive model.

variants.name: Myaede (Nefa Coilguns)
variants.description: The Myaede is neither elegant nor fast, but it has remained the mainstay of Successor commerce since before the collapse of the old empire over a thousand years ago, boasting a spacious cargo hold, heavy armor, and a flexible enough weapons layout to let it fight back in a pinch. Much like the grand heirlooms of the High Houses, a familial Myaede is often passed down through the lineage of spacefaring low-born Successors, and many of the pilots flying these first took the helm as children under a grandparent's watchful gaze.

variants.name: Spring Leaf (Jump)
variants.description: This ancient Wanderer transport was among the ships originally in use when they first arrived in our galaxy. Now, obsolete, the Spring Leaf is best suited for display in a museum.

variants.name: Autumn Leaf (Hai Crew)
variants.description: The Autumn Leaf is based on the Wanderer Summer Leaf light warship, but slightly larger and better equipped for combat. Unlike Wanderer peacetime ships, it is equipped with a turret mount in addition to the ports for fixed guns.

variants.name: Autumn Leaf (Missile)
variants.description: The Autumn Leaf is based on the Wanderer Summer Leaf light warship, but slightly larger and better equipped for combat. Unlike Wanderer peacetime ships, it is equipped with a turret mount in addition to the ports for fixed guns.

variants.name: Deep River Pirate 0
variants.description: The Deep River is a modular freighter, designed to carry cargo in detachable pods.

variants.name: Deep River Pirate 1
variants.description: The Deep River is a modular freighter, designed to carry cargo in detachable pods.

variants.name: Deep River Carrier (Full)
variants.description: This is a Deep River freighter that has had some of its cargo container mounts modified to carry drones.

variants.name: Deep River Carrier (Half)
variants.description: This is a Deep River freighter that has had some of its cargo container mounts modified to carry drones.

variants.name: Deep River Rapids (Turbo Blaster)
variants.description: This is a Deep River freighter that has been converted into a war ship.

variants.name: Deep River Rapids (Deep River Pirate 4)
variants.description: This is a Deep River freighter that has been converted into a war ship.

variants.name: Deep River Rapids (Deep River Pirate 3)
variants.description: This is a Deep River freighter that has been converted into a war ship.

variants.name: Deep River Rapids (Deep River Pirate 2)
variants.description: This is a Deep River freighter that has been converted into a war ship.

variants.name: Derecho (Advanced Cooling)
variants.description: Like a latent gene waiting to express itself, the knowledge of how to wage war in space has been passed down through hundreds of generations of Wanderers. Based on one of their ancient designs, the Derecho has a mixture of agility and raw firepower that is well-suited to their present, rapidly changing situation.

variants.name: Derecho (Hai Crew)
variants.description: Like a latent gene waiting to express itself, the knowledge of how to wage war in space has been passed down through hundreds of generations of Wanderers. Based on one of their ancient designs, the Derecho has a mixture of agility and raw firepower that is well-suited to their present, rapidly changing situation.

variants.name: Flycatcher (Laser)
variants.description: Flycatcher drones are used by the Wanderers to keep their star systems safe. Rather than carrying weapons of its own, a stock Flycatcher just carries an anti-missile turret for defending other ships. 	Drones do not come equipped with a hyperdrive. You cannot carry a drone unless you have a ship in your fleet with a drone bay.

variants.name: Hurricane (Advanced Cooling)
variants.description: The Hurricane is not built for speed, elegance, or versatility, but for one simple purpose: to be durable enough to serve as a rearguard, absorbing an enemy's attacks for long enough to allow the fleet it is guarding to escape.

variants.name: Hurricane (Hai Crew)
variants.description: The Hurricane is not built for speed, elegance, or versatility, but for one simple purpose: to be durable enough to serve as a rearguard, absorbing an enemy's attacks for long enough to allow the fleet it is guarding to escape.

variants.name: Shallow Pond (Jump)
variants.description: These ancient Wanderer interceptors can deploy a drone for added versatility in combat.

variants.name: Storm Seeker (Troops)
variants.description: An old relic from a time when the Wanderers occupied what is now southern human space, the Storm Seeker is a security patrol ship with an array of information warfare technologies built directly into the hull.

variants.name: Strong Wind (Hai Crew)
variants.description: The Strong Wind was originally designed for science and exploration, but recently the Wanderers have modified the design to allow it to be used as a warship.

variants.name: Strong Wind (Shields)
variants.description: The Strong Wind was originally designed for science and exploration, but recently the Wanderers have modified the design to allow it to be used as a warship.

variants.name: Summer Leaf (Missile)
variants.description: The Summer Leaf is mostly used by the Wanderers as a light transport, but it is also quite effective in combat.

variants.name: Tempest (Hai Crew)
variants.description: In response to the Unfettered invasion, the Wanderers have begun digging up ancient warship designs from their archives and putting them back into production. The Tempest is the first purpose-built warship they have manufactured in tens of thousands of years.

variants.name: Thunder Maker B
variants.description: An ancient Wanderer planetary defense system.

variants.name: Thunder Maker C
variants.description: An ancient Wanderer planetary defense system.

variants.name: Thunder Maker (Modern)
variants.description: An ancient Wanderer planetary defense system.

variants.name: Tornado (Jump)
variants.description: An ancient Wanderer warship, the Tornado was likely used to fulfill the same role as the modern Tempest. There are many similarities between the two ships.

variants.name: Tsunami (Jump)
variants.description: The Tsunami is a mobile fortress. Among the ancient Wanderer vessels, it was their closest equivalent to a city-ship.

variants.name: Winter Leaf (Jump)
variants.description: With the Unfettered Hai behind them and the unknown beyond the Eye ahead, Wanderer shipyards are prepared to phase out production of the Summer Leaf in favor of this ancient alternative.

variants.name: Storm Seeker Reborn
variants.description: An old relic from a time when the Wanderers occupied what is now southern human space, the Storm Seeker is a security patrol ship with an array of information warfare technologies built directly into the hull.

outfits.name: Pyrite
outfits.description: Also known as Fool's Gold, Pyrite is a common component in the manufacture of photovoltaic panels. It is also used in magnetic data storage technologies and non-rechargeable batteries.

outfits.name: Quantum Bloodcore
outfits.description: There is some speculation that Bloodcores only form from supernovas that resulted in the deaths of billions of sentient lifeforms. The presence of Quantumium in the system prior to the supernova may also be a prerequisite. But there is no way to test this hypothesis without actually witnessing a supernova take place in a system with those features and observing the result, which could take several millenia to crystallize.

outfits.name: Quantumium
outfits.description: The raw ore used to make Quantum Keystones. Since it has not been processed, it occupies more space than a Quantum Keystone does.

outfits.name: Deuterium
outfits.description: Deuterium is normally harvested from the cloudy atmospheres of gas giants. However, it can also be found frozen in the icy cores of wandering comets.

outfits.name: Fossil
outfits.description: An alien fossil found in the void of space. Unless you can find the right buyer, most will only see a cheap trinket that can be sold as a souvenir to gullible tourists. 	This is a rare relic. You can install it on your ship to keep it from getting mixed in with the regular cargo.

outfits.name: Mysterious Treasure
outfits.description: The old stories of pirates burying treasure in some out of the way dirt clod are true! While you can sell it anywhere for a modest sum, having it appraised by someone with knowledge of rare artifacts may yield better results. 	This may be a rare artifact. You can install it on your ship to keep it from getting mixed in with the regular cargo.

outfits.name: Earth Artifact
outfits.description: This is an artifact from Earth's distant past with some historical significance. You can sell it for a decent sum. 	This is a rare artifact. You can install it on your ship to keep it from getting mixed in with the regular cargo.

outfits.name: Alien Artifact
outfits.description: This is an artifact from an unknown alien civilization that once occupied what is now human space. You can sell it for a significant sum! 	This is a rare artifact. You can install it on your ship to keep it from getting mixed in with the regular cargo.

outfits.name: Space Junk
outfits.description: Centuries after they've ceased functioning, the wreckage of old satellites and probes can still be found littering space. The reward for recycling this junk isn't much, but if you won't do your part to keep the galaxy clean, who will?

outfits.name: Dysprosium
outfits.description: Dysprosium is never naturally found as a free element. Many industries in a spacefaring civilization have a use for it.

outfits.name: Krypton
outfits.description: Krypton is used in nuclear fusion energy research and experimental particle physics.

outfits.name: Radon
outfits.description: Radon is used in some radiation cancer therapies. Ironically, due to its radioactive properties, it is also a carcinogen.

outfits.name: Xenon
outfits.description: Xenon is the preferred propellant used by Ion Engines since it is more environmentally friendly and less corrosive than other alternatives.

outfits.name: Hackerz Plugin Omega
outfits.description: Installing this onto a ship should allow you to install one outfit that normally could not be installed due to reinstall. 	This cannot be uninstalled while the other outfit is installed, so use this with caution.

outfits.name: Hackerz Plugin Alpha
outfits.description: Installing this onto a ship should allow you to uninstall one outfit that normally could not be uninstalled due to integrated systems or fused circuits. 	This cannot be uninstalled unless the other outfit is installed, so use this with caution.

outfits.name: Hackerz Plugin Sigma
outfits.description: Installing this onto a ship disables its spinal mount. Why anyone would do this is unknown. 	This cannot be installed onto a ship that doesn't have a spinal mount or if something is already installed in its spinal mount.

outfits.name: Popcorn Box
outfits.description: A box filled with golden buttery popcorn to enjoy while watching a story unfold. 	Certain rare missions are more likely to trigger while this is installed on your flagship.

outfits.name: Rusty Asteroid Scanner
outfits.description: This rusty old asteroid scanner may look like junk, but it still works. Unfortunately the effective range is so low you might not realize an asteroid is minable until you're practically on top of it.

outfits.name: Emergency Repair Kit
outfits.description: This is a set of tools and spare material for repairing the hull. While impractical for use while engaged in combat, a ship with this installed can be repaired while landed on a planet that lacks hull repair services.

outfits.name: Gremlin Circuits
outfits.description: Some fused circuits from when you salvaged parts to make the Gremlin. You never got around to fixing it, but they're not connected to anything important so it should be fine...

outfits.name: Food?
outfits.description: This is barely edible, but it should be able to keep you going for another day.

outfits.name: Speck Access Temporary
outfits.description: This technical manual details how to manufacture Speck Rounds. Having this makes it possible for any outfitter to offer Speck Rounds even if it is normally not stocked there. 	The Aberrant threat has loosened any restrictions the Twilight Guard would normally have on sharing this technology. 	This tech can be researched instead of purchased. (Hover/Tap the attributes below for more details.) 	After this is acquired it can be found in the Licenses area in future visits to the outfitter.

outfits.description: This technical manual details how to manufacture Speck Rounds. Having this makes it possible for any outfitter to offer Speck Rounds even if it is normally not stocked there. 	The Aberrant threat has loosened any restrictions the Twilight Guard would normally have on sharing this technology.
